propositions: The test_ledger_attribution_is_unchanged_by_the_batching fixture setup intermittently fails at git merge with exit code 1 during pytest-xdist runs, but the failure is not a genuine content conflict.
The fixture creates hard-coded literals with byte-identical content in the shared path (1500-shared01-STATUS.json) on both branches, making a content conflict structurally impossible.
The _git() helper captures git output via capture_output=True but CalledProcessError.__str__ does not render stdout/stderr, destroying diagnostic information.

Exit code 1 from git merge can result from a content conflict, a failing pre-merge-commit hook, a failing commit-msg hook, or an unresolvable merge argument; the current error message does not distinguish among these.

Approximately 29,400 test executions including 1500 serial replays of the exact git sequence, 40 module runs, 72 concurrent module runs, and 3 full test rounds under xdist produced zero reproductions of the failure.
The fix surfaces git stderr and stdout in the CalledProcessError message and remains catchable as subprocess.CalledProcessError, enabling future occurrences to be diagnosed.
